title: Queued runs keep advancing when the registry cannot be read at job end
lead: S05 (landed 67521b0) starts queued runs when a job ends. launchRun's job goroutine reads the registry for the caps (internal/daemon/runs.go:409-413). If that read fails, it prints "start queued runs: ..." to stderr and starts nothing. The queued runs then wait until another job ends or the daemon restarts. The daemon stays up, because a queued run counts as active. Noted in the S05 run report as a low-severity choice for the owner.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A transient registry error (a half-written projects.json, a read error) leaves queued runs stuck with free slots and no message beyond one stderr line.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/daemon/runs.go`: launchRun (:389-417), startQueuedLocked (:352-387), hasRoomLocked (:326-350), runManager.
- `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: a test beside the S05 wave tests.
- `docs/design.md`: Wave lifecycle step 5 (:155-157), only if the behavior it states changes.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- With a free slot and a queued run, a job ends while the registry read fails: the queued run still starts (proposed; the owner decides the behavior, see Implement).
- With the registry unreadable and no earlier good read, the queued run stays queued and a later job end that can read the registry starts it.
- The S05 tests still pass (TestQueuedRunStartsWhenASlotFrees).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Cache the last good registry in runManager: set it on each successful registry read and use it when the read fails at job end (startQueuedLocked, hasRoomLocked). With no earlier good read, leave the queued run queued so a later job end that can read the registry starts it. Write the failing tests first and watch them fail. Decided 2026-10-23 (owner interview): cache the last good registry. Nothing is open.
